Hi Laura —

Thanks for the time last week. As promised, attached is our proposal for continuing BillStream as your primary billing provider. Highlights:
- 12-month renewal with volume pricing tiers; 18% savings if you commit to 36 months.
- Option to consolidate invoicing and revenue recognition exports into your NetSuite instance (we provide a lightweight connector).
- 99.95% SLA for core billing operations; premium support add-on available.

If helpful I can set up a deep-dive next Tue/Wed to walk the tech and finance teams through the integration points and timeline.

Best,

Folks — forwarding BillStream's proposal. Quick asks:
1) Rishi — can you run a TCO for 12 vs 36 months and include change-of-control exit costs? We need unit cost per invoice/token and projected run rate.
2) Marissa — please validate product fit: the connector description sounds lightweight but I want confirmation on revenue recognition edge cases (proration, credits, refunds).
3) Kim — can legal prep an NDA/SLA review slot? We may ask for a 60-day limited trial or pilot.

Goal: decide by 3/31 whether we: (A) renew BillStream as-is, (B) negotiate a shorter renewal with trial, or (C) consolidate more into NetSuite and put BillStream on a sunset path.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync Wed if that helps.

Laura / team —
I've attached an initial cost sheet comparing: current renewal (12m), extended (36m), and a partial consolidation scenario where we shift events ingestion/resolution to NetSuite billing while keeping BillStream for complex subscription billing. Key calls:
- Financially, 36-month commitment reduces annualized spend by ~16% after breakage assumptions; but early termination penalties (90 days) are material if we decide to sunset.
- The partial consolidation reduces per-invoice cost by ~9% but increases one-time engineering migration cost estimated at $120k (3–4 sprints).
- Recommend we ask BillStream for a performance credit clause and a 60-day pilot at no charge — this would de-risk the migration window.

If we want I'll draft a short memo for procurement outlining approval thresholds (>$250k requires VP+ finance exec signoff).

Rishi
Director, Finance Systems
rishi@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: BillStream renewal proposal + consolidation options

Couple of notes from a product/ops perspective:
- The BillStream connector they mention is common but doesn’t cover complex credit/adjustment workflows we run for enterprise customers. We should request a detailed mapping of their refund/proration handling and sample exports.
- Suggested technical agenda for the vendor deep-dive: 1) data model for subscriptions, 2) refund/proration flows, 3) webhook latency and at-least-once guarantees, 4) reconciliation reports for NetSuite.
- Timeline: if we want to keep options open, schedule vendor deep-dive next Tue (3/30) and target a procurement decision by EOD 3/31.

Also tagging Kim: please confirm if legal needs any specific language for the pilot (trial length, data retention, IP).

— Marissa
Head of FinOps
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: BillStream renewal proposal + consolidation options
Attachments: BillStream-SLA-draft-2027.docx (docx)

Elena — thank you and apologies for the internal thread. We reviewed the proposal and have a few next steps:
1) Please provide a sample export of subscription adjustments and a short doc on your proration/refund model (example CSV or mapping).
2) We want to do a 60-day pilot (no charge) scoped to our mid-market cohort and a mutually agreed success criteria list (reconciliation accuracy, latency, incident resolution time).
3) Please confirm you can accept a performance credit clause tied to monthly billing uptime and reconciliation accuracy.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your integration engineer on Tue 3/30 at 11:00 PT — invite sent.

We'll have finance and FinOps on the call. After the pilot we will decide whether to proceed with a 12-month renewal, pursue a 36-month discount, or move forward with consolidation into NetSuite.

Thanks — Laura
